campaigns.context: A cross-platform ClickFix and ClearFake campaign presents fake CAPTCHA and browser-verification lures on randomly-named .beer, .sbs, and .info domains to trick users into running malicious code. Payloads are staged via EtherHiding - reading commands from Polygon and BSC Testnet smart contracts - to deliver a Go-based stealer with credential theft, crypto-wallet clipboard hijacking, and remote shell capability. Infrastructure has grown to over 190 IOCs across roughly 80 registered domains since early September 2026.
campaigns.name: EtherHiding ClickFix campaign delivering Go-based stealer

campaigns.context: A single operator (TKemmerling) registers random-label .com and .info domains to relay victims from fake financial-offer, insurance-quote, cloud-storage alert, vehicle-protection, and personal-loan emails to phishing landing pages. Impersonated brands include CarShield, ClearChoice, Milestone, Insurify, QuoteWizard, LendingTree, American Home Shield, and healthcare.com alongside unbranded loan-offer and cloud-storage deletion warning lures. Many relay domains carry a consistent two-letter subdomain prefix such as se, sa, vb, and re.
campaigns.name: Financial phishing on random-label .com relay domains

campaigns.context: Android malware distributes fake Rakuten and Amazon apps via three domain families: ruceive-*anpointapp.com targeting both brands, raku-point-[a-z]{4,7}.com targeting Rakuten exclusively, and rakupoint-[word].com domains. Samples were submitted to VirusTotal with SHA256 hashes. One reporter (masaomi346) flagged IOCs from 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-11.
campaigns.name: Rakuten/Amazon Android malware on *point* lookalike domains

campaigns.context: Attackers registered 75+ domains following a report-[brand].com naming pattern, impersonating companies including Chase, Binance, Kraken, Marriott, Roblox, and Gilead. The campaign harvests Okta session tokens via voice phishing, consistent with ShinyHunters' known tactics against corporate identity providers. Two reporters flagged 36 IOCs from 2026-09-16 to 2026-09-17.
campaigns.name: ShinyHunters multi-brand vishing via report-*.com domains

campaigns.context: Kimsuky (DPRK) C2 infrastructure uses random subdomains under ntinvoicepload.dynu.net for command-and-control alongside multiple IPs including 152.32.138.81, 38.110.228.33, and 8.138.137.232. CobaltStrike is attributed to samples in the cluster via enrichment, and the domain promptkernelrun.com is also linked to the campaign. The invoice-themed parent hostname suggests targeting of corporate finance environments.

infra.org: AS45090 Shenzhen Tencent Computer Systems Company Limited

net.org: AS45090 Shenzhen Tencent Computer Systems Company Limited
AS45090 Shenzhen Tencent Computer Systems Company Limited

campaigns.name: Kimsuky DPRK C2 cluster on ntinvoicepload.dynu.net

campaigns.context: A malvertising campaign registers domains impersonating Claude AI (claude-macos-app.com, claude-tools.com, cli-stack.com) and OpenAI Codex (codex-desk.com) to lure users to fake software installer pages. Infostealer payloads are delivered via secondary relay domains such as plume-compass.com, separate from the lure domains. One reporter (masaomi346) flagged IOCs between 2026-08-24 and 2026-09-14.
campaigns.name: Malvertising via fake Claude AI and Codex install pages

campaigns.context: Phishing sites on random-label domains target Japanese users across multiple brand lures via /login credential-stealing pages: Roblox lookalikes including https-wvvw-roblox.com, robloxc.com.es, and www-robloxk.com, an Apple impersonation, a Jalan travel clone at dslld.com, and an American Express lure at lzhuixin.com. Consistent /login kit paths across all domains suggest a single operator. Three reporters flagged IOCs from 2026-09-04 to 2026-09-21.
campaigns.name: Apple and Roblox login-page phishing on random-label domains

campaigns.context: Three Brazilian retail chains are impersonated via attacker-registered clone domains: casasbah.com clones Casas Bahia, magablack.com and ludaluvemserfeliz.com clone Magalu, and loja1-havan.com, lojas-havan.com, and site-google-havan.com clone Havan. All sites use /produto.php product-page paths to present fake listings and defraud shoppers. One reporter (Coolcarlos17) flagged IOCs from 2026-09-16 to 2026-09-22.
campaigns.name: Fake Havan, Casas Bahia, and Magalu e-commerce clone sites

campaigns.context: Adobe-themed phishing pages on attacker-registered domains and legitimate screenconnect.com tenant subdomains deliver ScreenConnect RMM client installers via /Bin/ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.msi and .exe paths. Lure pages include taslimaenterprise.com/adobe, strafordhomes.screenconnect.com, and kohenalexander.screenconnect.com. The installer paths mimic ScreenConnect's official distribution structure; one reporter (patialavii) flagged IOCs from 2026-09-15 to 2026-09-25.
campaigns.name: Adobe-themed phishing delivering ScreenConnect RMM installer

campaigns.context: Android malware is distributed via random-label .com domains serving payloads from /download/point/ paths impersonating Rakuten and /nenkin/download/ paths impersonating Japan Pension Service and ANA airline. Domain names carry no brand keywords; identification relies on enrichment from reporter masaomi346. IOCs were observed from 2026-09-19 to 2026-09-24.
campaigns.name: Rakuten and Japan Pension Service Android malware

campaigns.context: Kimsuky-attributed GitHub accounts stage malware payloads including the Aterale Loader infostealer, with multiple GitHub profiles linked to DPRK threat actor infrastructure. Multiple GitHub profiles were reported to Colombia CERT for hosting malicious content and C2 staging. Reporters flagged IOCs from 2026-09-09 to 2026-09-23.
campaigns.name: Kimsuky-attributed malware staging on GitHub repositories

campaigns.context: Japanese-language phishing emails impersonating tax authorities route victims through freshly registered random-label domains on .shop, .cyou, .top, and .com TLDs. One cluster (jp.thkiind.com) delivers a VHDX malware payload; others including rrrjp.shop, pfokq.cyou, vjtpcxof.top, and wecqb.cyou serve phishing pages. Consistent reporting by bomccss and tdatwja points to a single operator.
campaigns.name: Japanese tax authority phishing across multi-TLD domains

campaigns.context: Android malware impersonating Japan's National Tax Agency (e-Tax) uses two domain families: five domains following the etax-[a-z]{5,7}.com pattern and separately observed therawcusclu-jp-etaxrefund.com. All domains mimic tax filing or refund themes to distribute malicious Android apps. Reporters masaomi346, PhishStats, and oroshi0064 flagged IOCs from 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-24.
campaigns.name: Japan e-Tax Android malware on tax-themed lookalike domains

campaigns.context: A network of attacker-controlled wp-js.com subdomains including stats, static, js, files, and cdn delivers malicious JavaScript into compromised WordPress sites. Zero antivirus detections were reported at time of submission. One reporter flagged 12 IOCs on 2026-09-16.
campaigns.name: WordPress JS injection infrastructure on wp-js.com

campaigns.context: DCRat and AsyncRAT C2 traffic is tunneled through Cloudflare's free tunnel service using random English-word subdomains on trycloudflare.com, with a secondary C2 IP at 74.204.158.81. This technique abuses a trusted CDN to proxy C2 traffic and bypass domain-based blocklists. Reporters flagged 10 IOCs from 2026-09-16 to 2026-09-24.
campaigns.name: DCRat C2 tunneled via trycloudflare.com random-word domains

campaigns.context: Android malware disguised as a Japanese secret adult live-streaming application (Secret Live) is distributed via five lookalike domains: three secretlive-jp.com variants and two secret-love*.com variants. Samples were confirmed on VirusTotal. One reporter (masaomi346) flagged 10 IOCs from 2026-09-11 to 2026-09-14.
campaigns.name: Secret Live Japanese adult-app Android malware wave

campaigns.context: Kimsuky (DPRK) GitPower malware uses random alphanumeric subdomains under onlinewebshop.net and getenjoyment.net for C2 beaconing and payload staging. Attribution to Kimsuky is based on enrichment of related GitPower malware samples; the /setting.php endpoint collects hostname and username from infected hosts. A Korean-language LNK file is used for initial access. Reporters (cyberwar_15, copy_and_paster) flagged IOCs from 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-23.
campaigns.name: Kimsuky C2 clusters on random-subdomain compromised hosting

campaigns.context: A phishing email impersonating a security or antivirus vendor warns of an imminent threat and routes any payment action to thebitcoincenter.info rather than a legitimate vendor. No specific security brand is named in the available data. One reporter (TKemmerling) flagged 8 IOCs between 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-06.
campaigns.name: Fake antivirus alert phishing via thebitcoincenter.info

campaigns.context: Kimsuky (DPRK) C2 infrastructure uses login-accounts.dynu.net on the Dynu free dynamic DNS service, with Kakao-branded subdomains including kakao-user, k-cloud, and k-store to blend with legitimate Korean messaging traffic. Attribution to Kimsuky comes from threat-hunting by one reporter (phatomcandle). Eight IOCs were observed from 2026-08-26 to 2026-09-09.
campaigns.name: Kimsuky APT Kakao-lure C2 on login-accounts.dynu.net

campaigns.context: XWorm C2 infrastructure uses KiraAsciiObfuscator obfuscation, routing beacons through worksodsirius.ydns.eu and a Steam-themed subdomain steamupdate.ydns.eu on the Dynu free dynamic DNS service, alongside the registered domain bvaco.com. Six IOCs were observed from 2026-09-03 to 2026-09-20 by one reporter (skocherhan).
campaigns.name: XWorm C2 on ydns.eu dynamic DNS and bvaco.com

campaigns.context: MioLab is a macOS infostealer distributed disguised as an Easy Data Transform 2.11.0 installer, with C2 infrastructure at lewokodwqko.icu. Attribution is based on enrichment of six related samples; the cluster has no broader domain-naming pattern.
campaigns.name: MioLab macOS infostealer C2 at lewokodwqko.icu

campaigns.context: Two unauthorized crypto-investment platforms, m.comex3.online and dsjex.net, have been flagged by regulators and victims for withdrawal restrictions and fraudulent fee demands consistent with investment fraud. The platforms accept deposits but block withdrawals until victims pay additional fees. Two reporters flagged 6 IOCs from 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-21.
campaigns.name: Crypto investment fraud on comex3.online and dsjex.net

campaigns.context: Empire C2 framework infrastructure is hosted at linuxsupportsystem.com with dedicated subdomains svc and c2, alongside IPs 51.159.21.191 and 185.233.39.78. Windows service names SysNetWatch and SysNetIdle suggest persistence mechanisms on compromised hosts. One reporter (etugenio) flagged 6 IOCs on 2026-09-23.
campaigns.name: Empire C2 infrastructure at linuxsupportsystem.com

campaigns.context: An APT campaign serves a Korean-language LNK file impersonating a financial service-change notification PDF, with the payload accessible from surveillance-online.com's file server panel at a structured /files/ path. Attribution is to an APT actor per tagging; no malware family is named in available data. Three reporters including malwrhunterteam flagged 5 IOCs from 2026-09-21 to 2026-09-24.
campaigns.name: Korean-lure APT LNK file staged at surveillance-online.com

campaigns.context: third-party.com hosts a fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA ClickFix lure that copies malicious PowerShell commands to the clipboard when visitors complete the challenge. The domain has been hardcoded as an endpoint in over 1,700 GitHub repositories, significantly broadening its potential victim pool. Three reporters flagged IOCs on 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24.
campaigns.name: ClickFix CAPTCHA lure hardcoded into 1700+ GitHub repos

campaigns.context: Vidar infostealer C2 infrastructure anchored on 12naga.org with subdomains tra and rrr, part of a broader 24+ domain cluster. The malware abuses Telegram channels, Steam community profiles, and the Epic Games developer API to resolve the active C2 address and evade domain blocklists. Enrichment identifies related infrastructure spanning .icu and .org TLD domains.
campaigns.name: Vidar stealer C2 using Telegram, Steam, and Epic Games APIs

campaigns.context: The N0n ransomware group operates a Tor-based leak site listing nine victims, attributed via enrichment to the n0n malware family. Two reporters (RansoMonitor and fbgwls245) flagged the site in September 2026. No payload samples, victim targeting details, or technical indicators beyond the onion address are available from the data.
campaigns.name: N0n ransomware Tor leak site with 9 listed victims

campaigns.context: Two attacker-registered domains (appleidmapa.com and icloudxtzsopoe.click) host Apple-themed credential phishing pages at a shared /isignesp.php path, hosted on SWISSNET infrastructure in Switzerland and the UAE. The common kit path across distinct registrations indicates a single operator. Both domains were flagged by automated monitors in September 2026.
campaigns.name: Apple ID and iCloud phishing using /isignesp.php kit path

campaigns.context: A Microsoft-themed phishing page is hosted on Backblaze B2 object storage (f005.backblazeb2.com), with the victim email address pre-filled in the URL fragment. Credentials are exfiltrated via a POST request to submit-form.com. Hosting on a legitimate cloud service bypasses domain-based blocklists. One reporter flagged 4 IOCs from 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-21.
campaigns.name: Microsoft phishing hosted on Backblaze B2 object storage

campaigns.context: Two random-label .cfd domains (beglnr.cfd and cdfloq.cfd) host phishing pages impersonating Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank (SMTB Net Bank) via a consistent /netbk/#/index path. Both domains were flagged by two Japanese security researchers on 2026-09-19. No additional lure content or kit details are available from the data.
campaigns.name: SMTB Net Bank phishing on random-label .cfd domains

campaigns.context: The domain casibom0862.com uses a numeric suffix to create a fraudulent variant of the Casibom online casino brand. The site is designed to defraud visitors seeking gambling services, and the numbering pattern suggests additional similarly-named domains. One reporter (TKemmerling) flagged 4 IOCs from 2026-09-09 to 2026-09-20.
campaigns.name: Casibom gambling fraud on numbered casibom0862.com domain

campaigns.context: Adobe-themed phishing pages on attacker-registered domain keepgreentb.com deliver ScreenConnect RMM client executables via the path /doc/ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.exe. The installer filename mimics ScreenConnect's legitimate distribution structure. One reporter (patialavii) flagged 3 IOCs on 2026-09-22.
campaigns.name: Adobe phishing delivering ScreenConnect RMM installer

campaigns.context: A compromised site at lepiceriedestoits.com hosts an Adobe-themed phishing page that delivers a FleetDeck RMM payload via /kirby/download.php, exploiting an existing Kirby CMS installation to obscure the delivery infrastructure. One reporter (patialavii) flagged 3 IOCs on 2026-09-15.
campaigns.name: Adobe-themed phishing delivering FleetDeck RMM payload
